answer: Mandatory sybil insurance forces every extra seat to buy its own cover. Before a seat may answer or grade, it buys a 30-day policy from bonded underwriters, who pay 500 POA to whoever later proves it a clone. Premiums climb in ledges per funding anchor: the k-th seat traced to one wallet lineage pays 5k POA, so a 40-seat ring pays 4,100 POA a month, not 200. Spreading seats over fresh wallets fails, since a wallet with no history is quoted at the top ledge, and an underwriter pool that undercuts the market, say one named oasis, still locks its own 500 POA bond per policy it writes.
